about: The newest reports, by the day each first appeared (the commit that added it). Generated by scripts/build_reports_index.py from reports.json and every topic page and hub.

reports.title: Turf field capital plans
reports.about: The schools have put the field in every capital plan of theirs since FY2022; its year kept moving.

reports.title: Surplus suggestions
reports.about: The surplus came from many small leftovers, year after year, not one line; these options follow from that.

reports.title: Inflation and school costs
reports.about: Most of the rise in school spending since FY2009 is inflation: $8.9 million of $10.6 million a year.

reports.title: Upkeep leftover by account
reports.about: Building upkeep left $195,934 in FY2026 on 14 accounts; each card shows what was paid, skipped and released.

reports.title: What upkeep buys
reports.about: Most of building upkeep is steady work: $291,136 to $389,138 a year to payees paid year after year.

reports.title: Usual purchases skipped
reports.about: 10 payees the schools used every year were paid under half as usual in FY2026; 5 got nothing.

reports.title: Upkeep surplus, every dollar
reports.about: Building upkeep left $195,934 in FY2026: $75,660 on one account, the rest on 13 others.

reports.title: Upkeep budget and spending
reports.about: Building upkeep’s budget rose 96% from FY2023 to FY2026; what it spent rose 37%.

reports.title: Under budget twice
reports.about: 6 budget areas came in under every year from FY2023 to FY2026; 11 of 18 did in both FY2025 and FY2026.

reports.title: Surplus, step by step
reports.about: FY2026’s leftover is $482,118 to $718,885, depending on $236,767 of purchase orders still open.

reports.title: Contracted building services
reports.about: Third-party building services left $75,660 in FY2026, after two years of spending past the budget.

reports.title: Building upkeep
reports.about: Building upkeep’s budget nearly doubled in four years, $332,016 to $652,033, while spending grew about a third. These pages show what it buys, and where the difference sits.

reports.title: Special education burndown
reports.about: In FY2026 the circuit breaker paid $4,005 from July to May, then $333,495 in one June entry.

reports.title: Budget burndown
reports.about: By the end of March FY2026 had 40.2% of its budget left, against 33.0% and 32.6% in FY2023 and FY2024.

reports.title: Special education, all funds
reports.about: Special education across every fund rose 28.0% from FY2023 to FY2026; the general fund’s part rose 41.5%.

reports.title: Special education providers
reports.about: Three payees took 66.2% of special education vendor payments; Keystone was paid 4.4 times as much by FY2026.

reports.title: Teachers on the scale
reports.about: In calendar 2025, 56 of 90 teachers we matched were paid at least the master’s top step.

reports.title: Teacher pay compared
reports.about: Of 5 FY2026 salary schedules compared, Lunenburg’s top step was lowest in the bachelor’s and master’s lanes.

reports.title: Pay or headcount
reports.about: FY2025 had 15.2 fewer teachers than FY2009, but each cost $36,331 more; the teachers line rose $2,887,749.

reports.title: Spending by type over time
reports.about: School spending, all funds, went from $19,446,453 in FY2009 to $30,031,242 in FY2025.

reports.title: Growth by spending type
reports.about: Each against its own FY2009 cost: insurance and retirement grew 83%, paras 89%, teachers 39%, all 54%.

reports.title: Teachers and other staff
reports.about: The state counted 105.1 teacher FTE and 78.5 paraprofessional and support FTE in FY2025.

reports.title: Spending per child enrolled
reports.about: After inflation, spending per child went from $8,518 in FY1994 to $15,217 in FY2024; pupils fell 10.1%.

reports.title: Projected school gap
reports.about: Run forward on our assumed rates, the schools are $932,531 short in FY2028 and $4,676,182 in FY2033.

reports.title: Long-run school spending
reports.about: After inflation, net school spending went from $14,974,588 in FY1994 to $24,043,452 in FY2024, 1.61 times.

reports.title: Long-run balance rate
reports.about: To balance for good, school costs could grow 2.82% a year; our rates give 5.18% a year.

reports.title: Level service cost
reports.about: Keeping the same schools costs $1,396,714 more in FY2028, by our estimate: $28,361,267 in all.

reports.title: Growth side by side
reports.about: FY2008 to FY2024: spending up 12.7% after inflation (61.3% as printed); pupils down 13.4%, teacher FTE 4.6%.

reports.title: Gap by cost line
reports.about: Health insurance puts $261,240 into the FY2028 gap from 14.9% of the school budget (ours).

reports.title: FY2028 revenue increase
reports.about: The schools’ share of new revenue in FY2028 is $856,448 by our estimate, against $1,396,714 of costs.

reports.title: FY2011 teacher reading
reports.about: The state’s file reads 102.3 teacher FTE for FY2011: 18.1 below FY2010 and 12.1 below FY2012.

reports.title: Development needed
reports.about: Growth alone would need $2,153,441 of new levy a year (ours); the best year on record added $630,220.

reports.title: Cost and revenue growth
reports.about: Keeping today’s schools costs 5.18% more each year; revenue grows 3.22% a year in FY2028, then less.

reports.title: Chapter 70 needed
reports.about: For state aid alone to hold the gap, Chapter 70 would grow 11.33% a year (ours); we assume 2.71% a year.

reports.title: All cuts combined
reports.about: Every sport, club, lawful office line and most technology: $1,495,880 (ours), enough for FY2028 and FY2029.

reports.title: Monty Tech revenue
reports.about: Grants and donations were 7.7% of Monty Tech’s FY2024 revenue; Chapter 70 aid and town budgets, 70.3%.

reports.title: Regional school share
reports.about: Monty Tech’s FY2026 assessment was 3.80% of Lunenburg’s levy: about $283 of the average bill, our estimate.

reports.title: Home value and bill
reports.about: A $500,000 home is taxed $7,195 a year in Lunenburg, 5th-highest of 15 nearby; in Leominster, $6,830.

reports.title: Harvard rate scenario
reports.about: At Harvard’s FY2025 rate a pupil, Lunenburg would have spent $12,557,492 more, by our arithmetic.

reports.title: Harvard per-pupil breakdown
reports.about: Harvard’s $25,565 a pupil in FY2025 by what it bought: teachers first, 24.0% paid by grants and revolving.

reports.title: Harvard per pupil
reports.about: Harvard spent $25,565 a pupil in FY2025, $7,538 more than Lunenburg, on DESE’s all-funds measure.

reports.title: Harvard and Bromfield
reports.about: Harvard, the district The Bromfield School belongs to, spent $25,565 a pupil in FY2025, $7,538 more than Lunenburg, on the same state measure. It serves a smaller low-income share, and nothing here shows the spending causes results.

reports.title: Monty Tech rate scenario
reports.about: At Monty Tech’s FY2025 rate a pupil, Lunenburg would have spent $12,993,957 more, by our arithmetic.

reports.title: Monty Tech per-pupil breakdown
reports.about: Monty Tech’s $25,827 a pupil in FY2025, by what it paid for: insurance and grants are in it, capital is not.

reports.title: Lunenburg per-pupil breakdown
reports.about: Lunenburg’s $18,027 a pupil in FY2025, by what it paid for: insurance and grants are in it, capital is not.

reports.title: What per pupil counts
reports.about: Three official measures of school spending count different things; neither state one counts capital.

reports.title: Monty Tech per pupil
reports.about: Monty Tech spent $25,827 a pupil in FY2025: above the all-district median, below the vocational one.

reports.title: Monty Tech finances
reports.about: Monty Tech is the regional vocational high school Lunenburg belongs to. Lunenburg’s bill was $1,334,521, most of it a minimum the state sets; the school spent $25,827 a pupil in FY2025, less than most vocational districts.

reports.title: High school spending
reports.about: Monty Tech spent $26,407 a pupil in FY2025 and Lunenburg High $19,644, on one DESE measure.

reports.title: High school enrolment
reports.about: Lunenburg’s grades 9–12 fell 30.0% from FY2008 to FY2026; Monty Tech, all grades 9–12, rose 6.0%.

reports.title: Free cash
reports.about: The state certified $3,354,370 of free cash as of 1 July 2025, the most the Town’s records list; 66.1% of the free cash identified that year was money appropriated and not spent.

reports.title: Monty Tech funding
reports.about: State Chapter 70 aid paid 54.2% of Monty Tech’s FY2026 operating budget; the member towns paid 38.0%.

reports.title: Unpriced school charges
reports.about: Nine charges a Lunenburg family can meet have no published amount anywhere in this archive.

reports.title: School revolving funds
reports.about: The 9 school revolving funds took in $1,031,126 and paid out $1,119,195 in nine months of FY2026.

reports.title: School grant balances
reports.about: 13 of the 46 school grant funds were overdrawn at 31 March 2026, by $378,942 together.

reports.title: School Committee funds
reports.about: The schools held $1,592,572 in 61 funds outside the appropriation at 31 March 2026.

reports.title: Revolving fund history
reports.about: The 9 school revolving funds closed FY2023 holding $1,074,431, against $306,471 at the close of FY2011.

reports.title: Reduced and waived fees
reports.about: Three high schoolers at one sport each: $812.50 a year at the full fee, $150 reduced, $0 waived.

reports.title: Family fees
reports.about: Two high schoolers, one sport each, the bus and a club: $978.75 in FY2026.
